svg.aria-label: Diagram: how Security Hub CSPM turns control findings into a control status and control statuses into a security score, and which populations each step drops. The Compliance.Status field of a control finding takes four values. PASSED indicates the control passed the security check for the finding and automatically sets the workflow status to RESOLVED. FAILED indicates the control did not pass. WARNING indicates Security Hub cannot determine whether the resource is in a passed or failed state, for example when AWS Config resource recording is not turned on for the corresponding resource type. NOT_AVAILABLE indicates the check cannot be completed because a server failed, the resource was deleted, or the AWS Config evaluation result was NOT_APPLICABLE, in which case the finding is automatically archived. Three routes produce a pass without anything being remediated: if you have no resources corresponding to a control, Security Hub produces a PASSED finding at the account level; if you delete a resource corresponding to a control, Security Hub creates a NOT_AVAILABLE finding, archives it immediately, and after eighteen hours produces a PASSED finding because you no longer have resources corresponding to the control; and because control status ignores findings whose record state is ARCHIVED or whose workflow status is SUPPRESSED, suppressing all failed findings for a control makes its status Passed. Control status takes five values: Passed when all findings are PASSED; Failed when at least one finding is FAILED; Unknown when at least one finding is WARNING or NOT_AVAILABLE and none is FAILED; No data when there are no findings, including when a control is newly enabled, when all of its findings are suppressed, or when it is unavailable in the current Region; and Disabled when the control is disabled in the current account and Region, though its findings may retain a compliance status for up to twenty-four hours after disablement. The score is the proportion of Passed controls to enabled controls, where enabled controls for scoring purposes are those with status Passed, Failed or Unknown, and controls with status No data are excluded from the calculation. A panel records that the scoring page describes the summary score two incompatible ways: near the top it states the summary security score is the average of the standard security scores, while the worked example divides unique passed controls by unique enabled controls after noting that each control is counted only once across standards. On the page's own example the five standard scores of 88, 22, 15, 74 and 62 average to about 52 percent while the stated division of 357 by 515 gives 69 percent, a gap of seventeen points, and the deduplication method is the one the example demonstrates. A further panel records the asymmetry across accounts and Regions: if the status of a control is Failed in even one member account its status is Failed in the administrator account, and if it is Failed in even one linked Region its status is Failed in the aggregation Region, so failure propagates upward while a pass can arise from local absence. A closing panel notes the operational dependencies: AWS Config resource recording must be configured for control status and scores to appear, scores are generated only for standards enabled when the Summary or Security standards console pages are visited, first generation happens within thirty minutes and thereafter statuses and scores update every twenty-four hours based on the previous twenty-four hours of findings, enabling a new aggregation Region or updating linked Regions resets existing scores, and turning on consolidated control findings can take up to twenty-four hours to be reflected.
svg.title: Findings roll into a control status; control statuses roll into a score. Each step drops a population.
svg.text: “the proportion of Passed controls to enabled controls” — controls, not resources.
Everything surprising follows from that sentence, plus: a control with nothing to evaluate passes.
Compliance.Status — per finding
PASSED
also sets Workflow.Status to RESOLVED
FAILED
one of these fails the whole control
WARNING
“can’t determine whether the resource is in a
PASSED or FAILED state” — e.g. Config recording off
NOT_AVAILABLE
“a server failed, the resource was deleted, or the result
of the AWS Config evaluation was NOT_APPLICABLE”
Three routes to a pass with nothing remediated
1 · No resources
“If you don’t have resources corresponding to a control,
Security Hub CSPM produces a PASSED finding”
2 · Delete the failing resource
NOT_AVAILABLE, archived → “After 18 hours, you
receive a PASSED finding”
3 · Suppress the failed findings
“its status becomes Passed, which can in turn improve your security scores”
Control status — computed after dropping ARCHIVED and SUPPRESSED findings
Passed all findings PASSED · Failed at least one FAILED · Unknown a WARNING or NOT_AVAILABLE, none FAILED
No data no findings — newly enabled, or all findings suppressed, or “unavailable in the current AWS Region”
Disabled no checks performed — but findings “may have a value for compliance status for up to 24 hours after disablement”
→ suppress all findings and the control becomes No data, which leaves the ratio entirely.
The ratio, and what it excludes
score = Passed / (Passed + Failed + Unknown)
“Controls with a status of No data are excluded”
Disabled is not an enabled control, so also outside it
delete, suppress, disable — all three move it the same way
The summary score, described two ways
“the average of the standard security scores”
“dividing… unique passed by unique enabled”
357/515 = 69% — 17 points apart, same page
Failure propagates upward; a pass can be local absence
“If the status of a control is Failed in even one member account, its status is Failed in the administrator account”
“If the status of a control is Failed in even one linked Region, its status is Failed in the aggregation Region”
→ an org-wide green is an aggregate of local silences as much as local successes.
Operational dependencies
AWS Config recording is required for control status and for scores to appear — and unrecorded resource types
produce WARNING → Unknown, which sits in the denominator and not the numerator. You lose score where you see least.
Cadence — first scores within 30 minutes of visiting Summary or Security standards, then every 24 hours, from the
previous 24 hours of findings. A remediation does not show the same afternoon.
Resets — “enabling a new aggregation Region or updating linked Regions resets existing security scores”; consolidated
control findings can take up to 24 hours to be reflected. A reset and a decline look identical on a dashboard.
A good trend line for one account over time. A poor comparative metric between accounts.
Across a quarter in which somebody decommissioned a workload, it mostly reports how much there was to check.
